subjects.why: an aborted repair writes bytes_raw:0/bytes_returned:0 and the meter must CREDIT it at exactly zero, never drop it

mutation.replace:
if (entry.bytes_raw === 0 && entry.bytes_returned === 0) continue;
    const signed = entry.bytes_raw - entry.bytes_returned;

subjects.why: THE SHIPPED DEFECT, restored at its source: max(0, raw - returned) turns a call that COST bytes into one that saved nothing
folding an unsizeable refusal in as 0 reads as 'we refused nothing worth having'
dropping the inherited>0 rejection lets a resumed session claim ids a sibling worktree already held
count-both for a doubly-owned invocation id: no id is ambiguous, so two sessions each credit the same call instead of both refusing

mutation.find: for (const [id, groups] of owners) if (groups.size > 1) ambiguous.add(id);
mutation.replace: for (const [id, groups] of owners) if (groups.size > 99) ambiguous.add(id);

subjects.why: counts instead of populations — the control's own comment says the slug COUNT grows 1→2 here, so a count reads nothing
